correctness.rationale: In the n-1 sum hyperplane, every subset-indicator normal projects with squared norm a(1-a/m). Symmetry averaging fixes the uniform candidate center. Exact slacks yield squared distances d_0^2=4(n-1)/(n(n-2)(n+1)) and d_k^2=2(n-1)(k-1)(n-k)/(nk(n+k-1)). The latter sequence has at most one interior maximum and its smallest term at the co-singleton index; the difference d_{n-1}^2-d_0^2 has the sign of n^2-7n+8, switching from cuts to coordinates at n=6. In dimensions n=4,5, summing active cut inequalities forces all vertex degrees, and the unsigned incidence rank n proves center-locus dimension m-n; from n=6 all coordinate inequalities force the unique uniform center. Facets/halfspaces sourced to Edmonds and Chaourar. The included standard-library verifier passed 451620 assertions, not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The canonical spanning-tree polytope is a central object of convex and discrete geometry. Intrinsic Euclidean inballs naturally quantify interior robustness of its edge-incidence embedding. The exact jump from n co-singleton cut contacts and positive-dimensional incenter sets (dimensions two and five) to m coordinate contacts and a unique center at n=6 is a nontrivial structural classification, not a small numeric improvement or routine normalization. The theorem gives every optimal center in the exceptional cases and a short general proof.
